Summary of Evidence: The WHO guideline on non-surgical management of chronic primary low back pain in adults highlights the lack of trials for certain interventions, such as lumbar braces, belts, and supports, as well as operant therapy. Judgments were made based on the experience of guideline development group (GDG) members in the absence of synthesized evidence. Critical Outcomes: For chronic primary low back pain, critical outcomes include pain, back-specific function/disability, general function/disability, health-related quality of life, psychosocial function, social participation, self-efficacy, and adverse events. Equity and Human Rights Considerations: No evidence synthesis was commissioned for all adults or older adults. Judgments were based on GDG members' experience. Feasibility and Acceptability: No evidence synthesis was commissioned for all adults or older adults. Judgments were based on GDG members' experience. GRADE Assessments: Risk of bias was downgraded due to unclear or high risks in random sequence generation, allocation concealment, blinding, incomplete outcome data, selective reporting, and compliance with interventions. Imprecision was downgraded due to small sample sizes and wide confidence intervals. Inconsistency was not assessed in cases with only one study.
